# Abrams distance-contrast successor r1 (`e880df5b…`): final review

**Verdict:** At 128px this is a real, moderate improvement over the fallback in the top, front-¾ and front views. The side views show essentially no gain. I found no holes, no regression and no unresolved objection in the three visual core categories. Production integrity stays open until the native masks finish and I can confirm the dimension result. This is not an approval.

## Files actually viewed

- **This turn:**
  - `distance-contrast-20261028/pbr-r1.png`, `recognition-r1.png` and `recognition-128-r1.png`
  - Native frames from `render-r1.json`: `top.png`, `front-three-quarter.png` and `left.png`
- **Not viewed:** the native contact sheet. Its path wasn't in the first 70 lines of `render-r1.json` (947 KB). I also didn't open the native `front`, `right` or `rear-three-quarter` frames; I saw those views only in the PBR sheets.
- **Fallback comparison:** `../readability-20261028/pbr-r1.png` and `recognition-128-r1.png`, which I viewed earlier in this session. I didn't re-open them this turn.
- **JSON:**
  - `component-plan-v3.json`, `validation-r1.json` and `catalog/rubrics/model-quality/1.0.0.yaml`, read in full
  - `export-audit-r1.json`: summary and the first checks only
  - `dimension-r1.json`: header and scope only. **I did not see its pass/fail result.**

## Neutral observations, before reading the plan

- **Top (native):** The roof is a continuous light zone running from behind the mantlet to the blow-off panels. The cheeks form a mid-brown V that frames a dark mantlet square at the root of the gun. The hatch lids are mid-brown discs with dark rims, periscopes and handles, so they read as closed lids, not openings. The hull deck is similar in value to the roof, so the turret-to-hull separation from above still comes mostly from outline and cheeks.
- **Front ¾ (native):** The mantlet reads as a distinct dark block between the cheeks. The roof, cheeks and hull separate in value. The tank reads coherently, not as patchwork.
- **Left (native):** The turret side shows the dark front cheek, then a narrow light vertical strip (about x 545–585), then the mid-toned stowage and bustle side. The hull and running gear are unchanged.
- **Front (PBR):** The mantlet is a darker square, now distinct from the cheeks. The flat black track blocks and the dark lower glacis band are unchanged from the fallback.

## Distance verdict against the fallback

| View | 128px change |
|---|---|
| Top | **Clearly better.** The dark V of cheeks and mantlet against the light roof is visible. The hatches are small mid-tone blobs, not black holes. |
| Front ¾ | **Better.** A dark notch at the mantlet is visible. |
| Front | **Slightly better.** The mantlet reads as darker. |
| Physical left/right | **No meaningful change.** |
| Rear ¾ | Marginal at best. |

- **Holes:** None. The mid lids (0.36) don't read as openings at 1000px or 128px.
- **Patchwork:** None, in my judgment. The three values follow the object boundaries, and the alternating roof bands I warned about are gone. Some viewers could read the cheek and roof contrast as a two-tone scheme. I don't treat that as a defect.
- **False joints:** The light strip on the left side follows a real gap between the cheek and the stowage box, so I count it as minor, not a fabricated seam.
- **Regression:** None seen. The roof highlights have a little less contrast but are still visible in `top.png`.

## Core categories: strongest below-3 objection for each

| Category | Score | Strongest objection | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| identity-recognition | **3** | The gain is confined to the top and front views. The side views at 128px are unchanged. | Resolved: identity cues are present in all six views at 256px. |
| silhouette | **3** | Unchanged from the fallback, since this was a material-only pass. The thin antennas still dominate the front outline. | Resolved: there is no silhouette regression. |
| mechanical-coherence | **3** | The darker mantlet makes the inherited mantlet box more prominent. The left side shows a narrow light strip. | Resolved: both follow real component boundaries and read plausibly in `front-three-quarter.png` and `left.png`. |
| production-integrity | **Not scored** | The native masks are pending, and I haven't seen the dimension pass/fail result. | **Unresolved.** It has support from the export audit (260 meshes, 7 planned paint substitutions only, non-paint faces unchanged, 10 materials, 36,408 triangles) and from `validation-r1.json` (passed, no issues, deterministic). |

## All 8 model-quality categories (static source; 3 means production-ready)

| Category | Score | Note |
|---|---|---|
| identity-recognition (core, 20) | 3 | |
| proportion-mass (15) | 3 | Unchanged geometry. |
| silhouette (core, 15) | 3 | |
| form-hierarchy (15) | 3 | The tonal zones now rank roof, cheeks and mantlet. Roof and hull deck values are close in the top view. |
| mechanical-coherence (core, 15) | 3 | |
| surface-material (10) | 3 | Value boundaries follow construction. Rubber, steel and glass are unchanged. |
| viewpoint-robustness (5) | 3 | The weakest views are the side views, with no gain, and the front view, with flat black tracks. Both are still intentional and grounded. |
| production-integrity (core, 5) | — | Pending masks and the dimension result. |

If production integrity also comes out at 3, the weighted total is **exactly 75, the go threshold**, with no margin. That's a scoring fact, not a `go`. Only the deterministic evaluator can issue that.

**Status:** `technicalValidation` passed for export and validation, with masks pending. `visualRecommendation` is no unresolved visual core objection from me, with structured evaluation and the production-integrity evidence still needed. `humanApproval` is none.
